vo: If God knew Samson would throw it all away, why did He give him so much strength?
He knew Samson would chase a Philistine wife his parents didn't want.
He knew Samson would tell Delilah how to take his strength away.
And still He gave him the strength to tear a lion apart and strike down a thousand men with a jawbone.
The clue is what the angel of the LORD told his mother before he was born.
"He shall begin to save Israel from the hand of the Philistines."
But notice: it doesn't say he'll save Israel. It says he'll begin to.
Which means Samson's job was to start the fight. Israel wasn't fighting back.
Even his own people tied him up to hand him over to the Philistines.
And that wife? It sounds wrong to us, but the marriage was part of God's plan.
"It was from the LORD, for he was seeking an opportunity against the Philistines."
Samson wanted a wife. God wanted to free His people.
So God didn't give Samson strength because he deserved it. He gave it because Israel needed saving.
Samson's choices cost him his eyes. But at the end, he prayed, "strengthen me only this once."
God answered, and the temple came down. He killed more Philistines in his death than in his whole life.
Samson started the rescue. Later, King David "defeated the Philistines and subdued them."
And the New Testament still lists Samson among the faithful.
So why give Samson so much strength? Because it wasn't about Samson. It was about the people God was saving.
So the next time you think you've messed up too much for God to use you… remember Samson.
